references.text: Moses sent the spies into the Negev region, which is mentioned here as they traveled up through it.
Hebron is noted as the place where Sarah died and Abraham purchased a burial site, highlighting the city's historical significance.
Hebron (Kiriath-arba) is mentioned as the place where Isaac lived, confirming the city's importance in the history of the patriarchs.
Joshua destroyed the Anakim from Hebron and other cities, referring to the same descendants of Anak mentioned here.
Caleb drove out the three sons of Anak—Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai—from Hebron, the same ones mentioned in this verse.
Judah defeated the Canaanites in Hebron and killed Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai, the same Anakim mentioned here.
Israel's fear of the Anakim, a great and tall people, refers to the same descendants of Anak that the spies encountered.
The Anakim are described as a large and numerous people, counted among the giants, providing background on who the spies met.
Zoan (Tanis) in Egypt is mentioned as the place where God performed wonders, confirming the city's significance in Egyptian history.
Zoan is noted as an important Egyptian city with princes and wise men, underscoring its historical importance compared to Hebron.
